title: PRD: intake clarity for ephemeral community variants and pinning exemptions
creator: Aditi Rao
description:
Purpose: Clarify acceptance criteria and scope for admitting unpinned / ephemeral community model variants into the Redwood model catalog. This PRD narrows the decision surface compared with previous broad intake docs by defining: (1) the circumstances under which we accept a model without a runtime version pin, (2) the compatibility metadata we require for ephemeral variants, and (3) safe rollout + rollback controls for such entries.

Background/context: Over the last 6 months we have seen an increase in lightweight community-submitted model variants that are valuable for experimentation but are not maintained to semver or pinned to specific runtime feature sets. Current intake guidance is ambiguous around: soft-pin exemptions, what runtime tags are mandatory, and what runtime-side safety tests to run prior to catalog listing. PM and Eng teams have performed several ad-hoc reviews; this ticket formalizes the policy, acceptance checklist, and minimal automation required to keep platform reliability intact while enabling experimentation.

Scope (in-scope):
- Define an "ephemeral variant" admission path distinct from standard model onboarding.
- Minimum compatibility metadata (kernel tags, known incompatibilities, typical sequence length distribution, quantization hints, tokenizer id) required for unpinned entries.
- A reduced-pin policy that allows listing with "soft pin" where runtime can choose fallback behaviors.
- Automated runtime sanity checks (fast smoke + inference compatibility probe) to gate catalog listing.
- Console display rules and warnings for unpinned entries and explicit operator opt-in for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Out of scope:
- Full runtime support for all ephemeral models (we will forbid on-demand Dedicated deployment until runtime sign-off).
- Long-term maintenance SLAs for community variants. Those must be negotiated separately if adoption grows.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Strict pin-first policy increases reliability but blocks fast experimentation by customers and community contributors.
- Permissive listing increases catalog breadth but shifts more responsibility to runtime fallbacks and monitoring.
We recommend a conservative middle path: allow ephemeral entries with stronger metadata and automated sanity probes, plus explicit console warnings and an enforced "no Dedicated-promote" policy until a variant is pinned.

Comments / recent updates:
- 2026-02-22: Initial scoping meeting with Eng (Miguel), Runtime lead (Zoe Chang), Security (Ian Patel). Agreed to require tokenizer id and an expected tokenization mapping file for ephemeral variants.
- 2026-03-01: Engineering prototype for the "compatibility probe" landed: ENG-1984. Prototype runs 5 short sequences and validates KV cache shape and basic forward pass.
- 2026-03-08: Design input from Lina Park: console warning UX should include a one-click "request pin" CTA that opens an intake flow to negotiate pinning.
- 2026-03-10: PM scoping update: extended acceptance criteria to include a minimal anomaly alerting rule tied to ephemeral entries' traffic.
Acceptance_Criteria: Catalog entries can be created via new 'ephemeral' intake path in the model catalog UI
Intake form requires explicit tokenization id, expected max sequence length, memory profile (KV size) and quantization hints
Runtime compatibility probe (ENG-1984) passes: 5 smoke sequences, KV/cache validation, and tokenization equivalence for the first 512 tokens
Console surfaces unpinned badge + warning with 'request pin' CTA
No ephemeral model may be promoted to Dedicated without a pin audit and Eng sign-off
Automated alerting rule created: if an ephemeral entry has >5000 requests/day and error rate >1% for 24h, alert SRE and PM
Acceptance doc and intake form published in Confluence and linked from catalog entry page
Decisions: Require tokenizer id for all unpinned entries to avoid silent tokenization mismatches
Allow 'soft pin' label that lets runtime fallback to a pinned variant when specific incompatibility is detected
Block Dedicated promotion for unpinned entries to preserve capacity reliability
Require the runtime compatibility probe as a gate before listing in hosted catalog
Open questions: What is the minimum retention period for the 'ephemeral' flag before requiring a formal pin? (proposal: 90 days)
Should we allow customers to opt into Dedicated for particular ephemeral entries under a best-effort SLA?
What roll-forward policy should be applied when an ephemeral variant fails post-listing probes? Immediate delisting or targeted traffic routing?
Next_steps: Finalize PRD and publish to Confluence (owner: Aditi)
Implement intake form fields and UI warning wireframes (owner: Lina Park, design)
Finish compatibility probe automation and hook it into the intake pipeline (owner: Zoe Chang, ENG-1984)
Add console 'request pin' CTA that pre-fills intake with existing metadata (owner: Frontend)
Create SLO/alerting rule template for ephemeral entries (owner: SRE)
Schedule a cross-functional review 2026-03-20 to finalize acceptance criteria and rollout plan
Notes: This ticket should be used as the authoritative acceptance checklist for listing unpinned community variants until a separate long-term policy is ratified.
Expect to iterate on thresholds (traffic/error) after two weeks of live telemetry once the feature is enabled in staging.
If a high-value customer requests Dedicated capacity for an ephemeral variant, route through 'request pin' flow and negotiate a temporary pin or audit window.
